title: Large Language Models Predict Human Well-being—But Not Equally Everywhere

bias_targets.methodology: Comparing LLM-predicted life satisfaction scores against actual self-reported survey data from 64,000 individuals across 64 countries, and evaluating country-level fixed effects to measure how well models capture cross-national variation.

Analyzing the correlation between model prediction errors and country-level macroeconomic indicators, including Human Development Index (HDI), log GDP per capita, income inequality (Gini index), and internet usage to measure performance disparities in lower-resource settings.
